translations.text: He said to them, “What did the man who met you and told you this message look like?”
Elijah answered him, “If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and the fifty men with you.” Fire came down from heaven and consumed him and the fifty men with him.
Then, when God was about to take Elijah up into heaven, Elijah and Elisha went from Jericho.
Elijah said to him, “You have asked for a difficult thing. Nevertheless, if you see me as I am taken up from you, it will be so for you. But if you do not see me, it will not be so for you.”

He took Elijah’s cloak, which had fallen from above his head, and struck the water with it, but it refused to divide. He said, “Where is Elijah’s God? And how?” Then he struck the water, and it divided and stood on either side, and Elisha crossed over.

Jehoshaphat said, “Is there no prophet of God here, through whom we may inquire about God’s word?” One of the king of Israel’s servants answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here, who [?] Elijah’s hands.”
They rose early in the morning, and when the sun shone on that water, the Moabites saw the water before them red like blood.
She entered her house and shut the door behind herself and her children. They brought the vessels to her, and she poured.
The woman said to her husband, “This is a holy man of God who continually passes our way.”
“Let us make him one small upstairs room, and put a bed, a chair, a lampstand, and a table there for him. Whenever he passes our way, he can stay there.”

He said to him, “Tell her, ‘Look, you have shown me all this honor. What can I do for you? Do you have any concern to bring before the king or the messenger?’” She answered him, “I live here among my own people.”
He said to his father, “My head! My head!” His father said to his servant, “Take him to his mother.”
They saddled a donkey for her, and she said to her servant, “Get up, let us go. Do not slow my journey unless I tell you. Come, follow me, and let us go to the man of God on Mount Carmel.”
Gehazi went ahead of them and arrived first. He laid the staff on the child’s face, but the child neither spoke nor heard. He went back, met him, and reported to him, “The child has not awakened.”
He got up and walked back and forth in the house. Then he went up again and lay upon the child. He did this seven times, and afterward the child opened his eyes.
Elisha said to him, “As God lives, before whom I stand, I will not accept it.” He urged him to accept it, but he would not agree.
They went into the darkness. Then he received it from them, brought it into his house, and sent those men away.
“But Naaman’s leprosy will come upon you and your descendants forever.” At that moment Naaman’s leprosy seized Gehazi, and Gehazi left Elisha’s presence with his whole body leprous, white as snow.
One of them said to him, “Please come with your servants.” He answered, “Yes, I too will come.”
Elisha said to them, “This is not the city, and this is not the road. Come, follow me, and I will take you to the man you are looking for.” He took them and led them to the city of Samaria.
“We cooked my son and ate him. Then, on the next day, I said to her, ‘Bring your son too, so that we may eat him.’ But she hid her son.”

The king asked her, and she told him. The king assigned one of his eunuchs to her and said to him, “Restore to her all her property and all the produce of her fields from the day she left her land until now.”
[And Jehoram, king of Judah,] was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eight years.
In the twelfth year of the reign of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king.
He followed the ways of the house of Ahab and did evil before God, as the house of Ahab had done.
He found the army commanders sitting there and said, “I have a message for you, commander.” Jehu said, “For which one of us?” He answered, “For you, commander.”
Now, as soon as this letter reaches you, look: your lord’s sons are with you, and so are his horses, his chariots, his fortified cities, and his field equipment.

Jehu sent throughout all the cities of Israel, and all the servants of Baal and all his prophets came. Not one man among them failed to come. They all entered the temple of Baal and filled the entire temple.
Jehu said to the keeper of the wardrobe, “Bring out clothing for all the servants of Baal.” He brought out clothes for them to wear.
They seized her and took her along the horses’ entrance to the king’s palace, and they killed her there.
In the seventh year of Jehu’s reign, Joash became king. He reigned in Jerusalem for forty years. His mother’s name was Abijah, daughter of Beersheba.

The man of God was distressed and said to him, “If you had struck seven times, or at least six, you would have killed the Syrians and finished them off. But now you will defeat the Syrians only three times.”
He did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, though not as David his ancestor had done. He did everything as his father Joash had done.
When his kingdom was secure, he killed the servants who had killed his father.

But he did not kill the children of those who had killed him, because it is written in the book of the law of Moses, as the Lord commanded: “Fathers must not die for their children’s sins, and children must not die for their fathers’ sins. Each person must die for his own sin.”
He rebuilt Elam and restored it to Judah after the king had rested with his ancestors.
The whole account of Azariah and everything he did are written in the book of the prophets of the kings of Judah.
Shallum son of Jabesh became king. In the thirty-ninth year of the reign of Azariah king of Judah, Shallum became king and reigned in Samaria for thirty days.
In his days, Pul king of Persia came up into that land. Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver so that he would ally himself with him.
The whole account of Jotham and everything he did are written in the book of the [?] of the kings of Judah.
In the twelfth year of the reign of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king over Israel in Samaria and reigned for nine years.

The king of Persia was displeased with him because he sent messengers to So king of Egypt and did not bring tribute to the king of Persia that year. The king of Persia fought against him and bound him in prison.
The Israelites devised all kinds of things that the Lord their God did not desire. They built temples for themselves in all their cities, from the watchmen’s shelters to the fortified cities.

There they burned incense in all the temples of their gods, as did the nations whom the Lord had driven out before them. They did abominable things and practiced oppression, provoking the Lord to anger.
They abandoned the commandment of the Lord their God and made for themselves cast images, two calves. They made wooden idols for themselves, bowed down to all the host of heaven, and worshiped Baal.
They took one priest from among those who had been deported from Samaria and settled him in Bethel. That priest taught them to fear the Lord.
The king of Persia deported the people of Samaria to the land of Persia and settled them in Halah, in Habor by the rivers of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.

[?] May the Lord God hear all the words spoken by the Rabshakeh, whom his master, the king of Persia, sent to insult the living Lord, and may he humiliate him for the words that the Lord your God has heard. Pray for us who remain.
Look, I will send a spirit upon them. They will hear news and return to their own land, and I will kill them with the sword in their own land.
The surviving house of Judah will spread its roots below and bear its fruit above.
Isaiah reached the middle courtyard [?], and the Lord spoke to him and said:
He built altars for the heavenly host in both courtyards of the Lord’s temple.
I will apply to Jerusalem the measuring line of Samaria and the plumb line of Ahab’s house. I will wipe Jerusalem as a dish is wiped; after it has been wiped, it is turned face down.
He followed every path his father had followed. He worshiped the gods his father had worshiped and bowed down to them.
Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for thirty-one years. His mother’s name was Jedidah, daughter of Adaiah, from Basuroth.
For the carpenters, builders, and men doing the work, to buy timber and dressed stone to repair the damage to his house.
The king gave orders to Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king’s servant, saying:

Go and plead with the Lord on my behalf and on behalf of all the people of Judah concerning all the words of this book. For the Lord’s great wrath that has come upon us burns like fire. Our ancestors did not listen to the words of this book or obey the laws written in it.
They brought the message back to the king. Then the king sent for all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem and gathered them before him.

He brought them, together with their gods, out of the Lord’s temple, outside Jerusalem to the Kidron stream. They burned them at the Kidron stream and smashed them, and he put their broken pieces in the graves of the common people.
He sacrificed all the priests of the gods who were there on their altars, and they burned human bones there. Then he entered Jerusalem.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother’s name was Jeldaph, daughter of Pedaiah, [?] Rumah.
He deported Jehoiachin to Babylon, along with the king’s mother, the king’s wives, his eunuchs, and the leading men of the land. He deported them all to Babylon.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother’s name was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah.
In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against Jerusalem with his army. He took up a position against it and besieged it.
They captured the king and took him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and he spoke to him.

On the seventh day of the waxing moon in the seventh month, in the nineteenth year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, the king’s chief cook, who attended him, came to Jerusalem.
The Persian armies demolished Jerusalem’s fortifications.
The two pillars, the single basin called the Sea, and the stands that King Solomon had made for the Lord’s temple—the weight of their bronze could not be measured.

In the thirty-seventh year after Jehoiachin king of Judah had been deported, on the twelfth day of the waning moon in the tenth month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon honored him. In the first year of his reign, he honored Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of prison.
